subject: gk
question: The office of Diwan-i-Insha dealt with which affair in administration?
solution:
The correct answer is __**State correspondence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Diwan-i-Insha **served as the correspondence department within the Delhi Sultanate, overseeing royal communications and the establishment of regulatory frameworks by the Sultans, which formed the foundation of law.
 
• Positioned as the third-ranking entity within the administrative hierarchy, it played a pivotal role in governance.
 
• At the helm of the Diwan-i-Insha was the Dabir-i-Khas, responsible for overseeing the department's operations.
 
• The Dabir served as the formal conduit of communication between the central authority and various regions of the empire, simultaneously holding the role of private secretary to the Sultan.
 
• The Diwan-i-Insha was tasked with drafting royal decrees and maintaining governmental records, ensuring the efficient functioning of administrative affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Delhi Sultanate, **also known as the Sultanate of Delhi, was an Islamic empire that flourished during the late medieval period, centered primarily in Delhi
 
• Spanning a duration of 320 years from 1206 to 1526, it held sway over vast regions of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• This empire emerged following the Ghurid dynasty's invasion of South Asia and witnessed the sequential rule of five distinct dynasties: the Mamluk dynasty (1206–1290), the Khalji dynasty (1290–1320), the Tughlaq dynasty (1320–1414), the Sayyid dynasty (1414–1451), and the Lodi dynasty (1451–1526).
